name: Career Mode
author: Sixth Front
description: Built into the game and always on: CAREER MODE on the main menu. Story missions for every kind of battle (infantry, tanks, aviation and naval), each career running from the First World War through the Second and the Cold War to the present day. A mission sets up its own battle, map, armies and weather, puts you in your seat and plays out a script: radio calls, waves, objectives, and the crew or section fighting beside you. Aboard the B-17G Lucky Lady, in a bomber stream of hundreds of Fortresses, you go from gun to gun on your feet through the inside of the bomber as the crew calls them (E leaves your gun, E takes the one you stand at), put out a fire in the radio room when she falls out of formation, then fly the bomb run over Schweinfurt through the Norden sight. Lead a cell of B-52Ds through the SAMs over Hanoi on the first night of Linebacker II, then fly a B-52H with GPS bombs over Afghanistan in 2001 for the Green Berets and the horse cavalry charging the Taliban line. Fly a Lancaster down to sixty feet over a reservoir at night and skip Barnes Wallis's bouncing mine into the dam until it breaks and floods the valley, and a Spitfire head-on into a raid of Heinkels and their Messerschmitts on Battle of Britain Day. Command HMS Lion at Jutland, a MAS torpedo boat against the Szent István, HMS Rodney against the Bismarck, HMS Prince of Wales when the Hood blows up in the Denmark Strait, HMS Ajax against the Graf Spee off the River Plate, the destroyer Johnston off Samar, in twenty-nine period warships. Fight a Centurion from the ramps above the Valley of Tears on the Golan Heights in 1973. Take the Indian Navy's missile boats into Karachi harbour at night in 1971. Break through to Bastogne in a Sherman in the snow, charge the 88s at El Alamein in the desert dawn, and hold the foxholes in the Bois Jacques under the tree bursts. Go over the top on the Somme in a Brodie helmet with a Lee-Enfield, take the guns at Brecourt Manor with an M1 Garand and TNT, hold Pavlov's house with a PPSh-41, and clear the streets of Hue with the Marines in 1968. Forty infantry missions, ten for each war, on ground made for each battle (hills, canals, jungle, mud, ruins): Mons, Anzac Cove, Fort Vaux, Caporetto, Passchendaele, Belleau Wood and Sergeant York; the Raate road, Edson's Ridge, Monte Cassino, Pegasus Bridge, Arnhem, Iwo Jima and the Reichstag; Chosin, Pork Chop Hill, Dien Bien Phu, Ia Drang, Long Tan, Ammunition Hill, Goose Green, Tumbledown and Hill 3234; Medak Pocket, Black Hawk Down, Takur Ghar, Nasiriyah, Debecka Pass, Fallujah, Sangin, Wanat, Kamdesh and Mosul. Forty tank missions, ten for each war, each era's tanks with their own models, guns and armour: Flers, Berry-au-Bac, Bullecourt, Fray Bentos, Hamel, Soissons, Musical Box and Saint-Mihiel; Stonne, Raseiniai, Mtsensk, Firefly, Arracourt and Cologne; the Bowling Alley, the Hook, Asal Uttar, Chawinda, Abu-Ageila, Basantar, the Chinese Farm, Dezful and Sultan Yacoub; Khafji, Medina Ridge, Basra, Objective Peach, Thunder Run, Fallujah, Wadi Saluki and Mosul. Forty naval missions, from Heligoland Bight, U-9, Coronel, the Falklands, the Q-ship and Zeebrugge to Dunkirk, Matapan, Guadalcanal, Convoy ONS 5, the North Cape and the Laffey, the Yangtze, Inchon, the Cuban quarantine, Tonkin, the Mekong, Latakia, the Belgrano and Bomb Alley, and the Red Sea; and forty aviation missions, from the Fokker Scourge, the airship over Cuffley, Bloody April and the Gothas to Pearl Harbor, Midway, Kursk and the Me 262, MiG Alley, Operation Focus, Bolo, Thud Ridge, Sandy, Mansoura, the Gulf of Sidra, the Bekaa and San Carlos, Task Force Normandy, the F-117 over Baghdad, the A-10s, Allied Force, Anaconda, Odyssey Dawn and the Red Sea drones, in some thirty more period aircraft. Missions open one after another; finishing one pays research points, silver and gold into the RESEARCH screen.
